chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up as a preacher and said, 'O people, beware of the green grass of al-Daman.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the green grass of al-Daman?' He said, 'The beautiful woman in the place of the ugly (or: from a lineage of the ugly).'

key_terms.خَضْرَاءَ الدِّمَنِ: Green grass of al-Daman (idiom for beautiful woman from ugly lineage)
key_terms.مَنْبِتِ السَّوْءِ: Place/lineage of the ugly (referring to family background)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'green grass of al-Daman' mean in Shia hadith regarding marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of 'green grass' (a lush, attractive pasture) to warn against marrying a beautiful woman from a family of the 'ugly' (often interpreted as those lacking in virtue, status, or religious piety). This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *kafa'ah* (compatibility), where physical beauty is balanced against the moral and social standing of the spouse's lineage, ensuring harmony in the marital bond.
